assertion: The EIA projected that power demand will rise from a record 4,216 billion kilowatt-hours (kWh) in 2025 to 4,306 billion kWh in 2026 and 4,370 billion kWh in 2027.
warehouse_value: US retail sales (ALL) 2025 4,058 BkWh; direct use excluded so not same measure
sql: SELECT price_year, sector_code, sales_million_kwh FROM energy.eia_electricity_prices WHERE state_abbr='US' AND sector_code='ALL'
reason: EIA estimate; matches the published STEO.

assertion: If correct, 2026 would be the third year in a row of record demand.
The EIA forecast that power sales in 2026 will rise to 1,546 billion kWh for residential consumers, 1,557 billion kWh for commercial customers and 1,061 billion kWh for industrial customers.
The all-time highs stand at 1,519 billion kWh for residential consumers and 1,503 billion kWh for commercial customers in 2025 and 1,064 billion kWh for industrial customers in 2000.
warehouse_value: US RES 2025 1,515, COM 2025 1,493, highest in 2006-2025 (preliminary vs STEO vintage)
independent_value: STEO 2025: 1,519 res, 1,503 comm, 1,050 ind (below 1,064); the 2000 industrial figure is not contradicted by anything found

assertion: the share of power generation from coal will slide from 17% in 2025 to 15% in 2026 and 2027, while the share of natural gas in 2026 will hold steady from 2025 at 40%, then ease to 39% in 2027.
warehouse_value: 2025 national generation: coal 16.6%, gas 40.8% of 4,430 TWh

assertion: The percentage of renewable generation will rise from around 24% in 2025 to 25% in 2026 and 28% in 2027, while nuclear power's share will hold at 18% in 2026 and 2027, the same as in 2025.

The EIA projected that gas sales in 2026 would slide to 12.2 billion cubic feet per day (bcfd) for residential consumers and 9.4 bcfd for commercial customers, but rise to 23.8 bcfd for industrial customers and 37.4 bcfd for power generation.

Those figures compare with all-time highs of 14.3 bcfd in 1996 for residential consumers, 9.9 bcfd in 2025 for commercial customers, 23.8 bcfd in 1973 for industrial customers, and 36.8 bcfd in 2024 for power generation.
independent_value: EIA history: 1996 residential 5,241,414 MMcf = 14.3 bcfd; STEO 2025 commercial 9.9, power 35.8 (below 36.8 in 2024). 1973 industrial high not independently confirmed but nothing contradicts it.

assertion: Demand is surging largely due to data centers dedicated to artificial intelligence.
inaccuracy: The claim says demand growth is largely due to AI data centers; EIA's STEO text says growth is driven by commercial-sector demand and hot summer temperatures and does not name data centers on the cited page.
